submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent (3.1e-7 A) among the three merit measurements. Composition Bi0.40 Cu0.19 V0.41 has Bi:V ~1:1, consistent with a Cu-modified BiVO4-type photoanode absorbing near 2.4 eV. Excess V (V2O5, MEGNet HSE gap 2.83 eV, on hull per MACE) or excess Bi both lowered performance.

rejected.reason: V-rich (V 0.57): measured 1.6e-7 A, half of index 268
Bi excess over V (Bi .44, V .36): measured 4e-8 A, steep drop off the Bi:V=1:1 line

consultations.verdict: Uninformative-to-mild support: MACE confirms V2O5 on hull, so V-rich compositions form stable vanadate matrices (BiVO4/Cu vanadate mix, gaps ~2-2.5 eV, absorbing at 2.4 eV). Index 10 sits at the center of the densely sampled V-rich region; good first anchor for GP.

MEGNet HSE gap of V2O5 is 2.83 eV, above the 2.4 eV photon energy, so V-excess regions gain little absorption from the binary. Moving to Bi:V ~1:1 (BiVO4-type scheelite, known photoanode, gap ~2.4-2.5 eV) with Cu ~0.19 is supported as a distinct exploration from the V-rich point (1.6e-7 A).

Mostly uninformative: MACE puts V2O5 on hull, and together with the earlier 2.83 eV gap this suggests excess V forms a wide-gap V2O5 phase that absorbs poorly at 2.4 eV. The measured trend (V-rich 1.6e-7 A below Bi~V 3.1e-7 A) points toward the BiVO4-type region with slight Bi excess. Index 93 (Bi .44, Cu .20, V .36) stays near the best point while testing that direction.
